verses.text: A song of ascents. When the LORD restored the captives of Zion, we were like dreamers.

xrefs.text: Also for you, O Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity.
[“]Yes, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem from captivity,
For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.

Behold, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the farthest parts of the earth, including the blind and the lame, expectant mothers and women in labor. They will return as a great assembly!
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!

verses.text: Then our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with shouts of joy. Then it was said among the nations, “The LORD has done great things for them.”

xrefs.text: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
Your righteousness reaches to the heavens, O God, You who have done great things. Who, O God, is like You?
And many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to plead before the LORD.”
Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from the nations, that we may give thanks to Your holy name, that we may glory in Your praise.

verses.text: The LORD has done great things for us; we are filled with joy.

xrefs.text: For the Mighty One has done great things for me. Holy is His name.
Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD. Wake up as in days past, as in generations of old. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced through the dragon?
When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass; then the hand of the LORD will be revealed to His servants, but His wrath will be shown to His enemies.
and on that day you will say: “Give praise to the LORD; proclaim His name! Make His works known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wasteland, Selah

verses.text: Restore our captives, O LORD, like streams in the Negev.

xrefs.text: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
A song of ascents. When the LORD restored the captives of Zion, we were like dreamers.
I will open rivers on the barren heights, and fountains in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.
Behold, I am about to do something new; even now it is coming. Do you not see it? Indeed, I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
Then the lame will leap like a deer and the mute tongue will shout for joy. For waters will gush forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.

verses.text: Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.

xrefs.text: Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.
Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God, for He has given you the autumn rains for your vindication. He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

verses.text: He who goes out weeping, bearing a trail of seed, will surely return with shouts of joy, carrying sheaves of grain.

xrefs.text: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.
Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.
For His anger is fleeting, but His favor lasts a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.

to console the mourners in Zion— to give them a crown of beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and a garment of praise for a spirit of despair. So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.
For this reason, they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
